title: A Day on Mercury Lasts Two Mercury Years
post_title: A Day on Mercury Lasts Two Mercury Years | QuantaTale
post_description: On Mercury, one sunrise-to-sunrise day lasts longer than two trips around the Sun. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://science.nasa.gov/mercury/facts/ https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/years-on-other-planets/en/ #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Mercury races around the Sun, completing a year in about 88 Earth days. But its slow spin and orbital motion combine to make one sunrise-to-sunrise solar day last about 176 Earth days. That means a single Mercury day-night cycle lasts roughly twice as long as a Mercury year. The distinction matters: one rotation relative to the stars takes about 59 Earth days, while the solar day is much longer.
